instructions:
1. Attach a single handle to a low pulley. Hold it in your left hand and step back to create tension.
2. Bend forward at the hips with your back flat and knees slightly bent. Rest your right hand on your right knee.
3. Let your left arm hang straight down toward the floor.
4. Pull the handle to your lower ribs, driving your elbow back and squeezing your shoulder blade in.
5. Lower the handle slowly under control, then switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and avoid rounding the spine.
2. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower.
3. Brace your core to resist twisting toward the cable.
4. Lead with the elbow, not the hand, to target the back.

instructions:
1. Set a pulley to mid-chest height. Stand side-on with feet just wider than shoulder-width.
2. Bend at the hips and knees and lean toward the floor. Rest your left hand on your knee.
3. Hold the handle in your right hand, arm extended out to the side at shoulder height, with a slight bend in the elbow.
4. Bring the handle across in front of your chest in a wide arc, keeping the elbow bend fixed.
5. Return slowly to the start under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight bend in your elbow throughout.
2. Squeeze your chest as the handle crosses your body.
3. Brace your core to resist twisting.
4. Move from the shoulder joint, not the elbow.

instructions:
1. Attach a single handle to a low pulley. Stand facing the machine.
2. Hold the handle in your right hand with your palm facing forward.
3. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and let your arm hang straight down.
4. Curl the handle up toward your shoulder, keeping your upper arm still and close to your body.
5. Lower slowly under control, then switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbow pinned to your side.
2. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
3. Squeeze the biceps at the top.
4. Avoid swinging the torso to lift the handle.

instructions:
1. Attach a single handle to a low pulley. Stand facing away from the machine and step forward to create tension.
2. Hold the handle in your right hand with your palm facing back.
3. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and let your arm hang by your side.
4. Raise the handle straight in front of you to shoulder height with a slight bend in the elbow.
5. Lower slowly under control, then switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Raise to shoulder height, no higher.
2. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.
3. Brace your core to resist twisting toward the cable.
4. Control the lowering phase, do not let the cable pull your arm down.

instructions:
1. Set a pulley to shoulder height. Stand side-on with your right side toward the machine.
2. Hold the handle in your right hand, arm extended out to the side at shoulder height, palm facing up.
3. Keep your upper arm parallel to the floor and still.
4. Curl the handle toward your head by bending your elbow.
5. Extend slowly back to the start under control, then switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arm fixed at shoulder height.
2. Squeeze the biceps at the top.
3. Exhale as you curl, inhale as you extend.
4. Move only at the elbow.
